Optional config decisions, no urgency: whether to push session transcripts to a separate repo instead of bolt-v2's origin (privacy call — full prompts/transcripts currently go to the code repo), and whether to decouple session-log pushes from code pushes. -> explain this

Both are about what happens to Entire's **session recordings** — the full transcripts of every AI session (every prompt you type, everything the agent says and does) that Entire saves as its record.

**Decision 1: where the recordings live.**
Right now they're stored *inside bolt-v2's own GitHub repo*, on a special branch. That means anyone or anything with read access to the code repo — the reviewer account, any future collaborator, any CI token — can also read complete AI conversation transcripts. Transcripts are riskier than code: they can contain pasted secrets, tool output echoing credentials, strategy discussion, etc. Entire has an open upstream issue acknowledging this exact concern. The alternative is a one-line config pointing recordings at a separate private repo made just for them; bolt-v2's repo then holds only code. **My recommendation: yes, do this** — it's a one-time setup (create one private repo, run one command), and afterwards I'd also delete the recordings branch already sitting on bolt-v2's GitHub so no transcripts remain in the code repo.

**Decision 2: whether recordings ride along with code pushes.**
Right now, every time code gets pushed, a hook pushes the recordings too. That coupling is exactly what made the 227 MB incident annoying: a broken *recording* interfered with pushing *code*. Turning it off means code pushes never touch recordings; the downside is recordings stop being backed up to GitHub automatically (they still work locally — search, recaps, explanations all function).

**How they interact / what I'd actually do:** if you take decision 1, decision 2 mostly stops mattering — recordings would push to their own repo, so a recording problem can no longer contaminate the code repo, and you keep automatic backup. So my overall recommendation is: **separate recordings repo, keep auto-push on, skip decision 2.** If instead you don't care about backing up recordings at all, the lazy alternative is decision 2 alone — one command, recordings stay purely local.

Verdict: **your instinct is right, and it's safe.** The facts:

- **36 of the 45 tracked SpecKit files are generated adapters** — the same 9 commands duplicated into four agent dirs (`.claude/skills`, `.gemini/commands`, `.opencode/command`, `.pi/prompts`). SpecKit's CLI regenerates them on demand from `.specify/` (the init options are recorded in the repo).
- **Nothing in CI reads them** — zero references in `.github/` or `.mergify.yml`.
- **AGENTS.md itself calls them "adapters"** and explicitly lists "regenerated adapters" as the sanctioned mechanism — the governance source of truth is `AGENTS.md` plus `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, not the prompt copies.

So committing them violates the repo's own single-source-of-truth stance: `.specify/templates` is the source; the 36 files are build output.

**My recommendation:**
1. **Remove the 36 generated prompt files** and drop the now-pointless allowlist lines (`!.claude/skills/`, `!.gemini/commands/speckit.*`, etc.) so all four agent dirs become fully ignored — anyone who wants the slash commands regenerates them locally and git never sees them. `.claude/` then answers your earlier question cleanly: ignored, entirely, no carve-out.
2. **Keep `.specify/`** — that's the actual SpecKit substance (templates, scripts, constitution), and AGENTS.md references it directly. Touching it would be a governance change, which is a different conversation.
3. Do it as its own small issue + PR per repo discipline (this is a workflow decision, not part of #1231's Entire fix), with the regeneration command documented in the PR body.
